cards.title: Concentration-Dependent vs. Time-Dependent Killing Patterns
cards.claim: The predictive PK/PD index is determined by the drug's killing kinetics. Concentration-dependent killing (rapid kill, regrowth below MIC) typically correlates best with AUC/MIC or Cmax/MIC. Time-dependent killing correlates best with fT>MIC. Time-kill studies provide initial insight into which index is likely predictive.
conditions: When selecting candidate indices for exposure-response analysis.
When interpreting in vitro time-kill data.
required_inputs: Time-kill study data showing organism numbers over time.
Observation of regrowth patterns relative to MIC.
Comparison of R² values for AUC/MIC, Cmax/MIC, and fT>MIC in exposure-response fits.
limitations: In vitro time-kill data supports its own analysis context but is not automatically animal efficacy.
Closely correlated indices may have similar fits; a small ranking difference alone does not establish a unique causal driver.
cards.downstream_use: Justification for index selection in PK/PD modeling.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
